about.title: Guadalupe Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Guadalupe is a small, tight-knit city, but that doesn't mean property owners get a pass when someone gets hurt on their floors, sidewalks, or parking lots. Whether the fall happened at a business along Guadalupe Street, in a lot off 11th Street, or on a poorly lit walkway near Rt 166, California law asks the same basic question: did the owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard, and did they fail to fix it or warn people? Proving that usually comes down to details — spilled liquid left too long, broken pavement never repaired, missing warning signs. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we connect injured Guadalupe residents and visitors with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, gather the store or building's records, and help you understand your options. There's no cost to get matched, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Notice and Evidence Early

items.title: Notice Is the Core Legal Question
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and didn't act. An attorney can help identify maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that speak to this.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Guadalupe businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having footage of the fall and having nothing.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Eliminate, Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for not seeing a hazard, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present the facts fairly rather than let an insurer overstate your share of blame.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Guadalupe?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit for premises liability. If the property involved is owned by a public entity — a city building or a Rt 166 rest area, for example — the deadline is much shorter and requires an early formal claim. Because these timelines vary, it's worth talking to an attorney soon after the incident.

items.question: What should I do right after falling at a business or on a sidewalk in Guadalupe?
items.answer: If you're able, photograph the hazard before it's cleaned up or fixed, note the time and weather conditions, and ask if there's a store manager or incident report. Given that many local crashes and incidents happen during busy weekday afternoons, businesses along Guadalupe Street and W Main Street may have shift changes that make witnesses harder to track down later, so getting names and details early helps.

items.question: Do I need to pay anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no fee to get matched and no obligation to hire anyone after speaking with an attorney.
